The two files declare five entities that match your filter:

- **`src/server/conversation/responseParser.ts`**
  - `scanFences` (lines 25–51) is a private module-level helper. It finds fenced code blocks in Markdown. If a `codeai-model` fence is never closed, it keeps it and marks it `unclosed`.
  - `parseAssistantResponse` (lines 53–93) is exported. It calls `scanFences` on line 55, then turns each fence into a `markdown`, `diagram` or `code` block.
- **`src/server/model/repositoryModelStore.ts`**
  - The `RepositoryModelStore` class (lines 12–41) holds a per-checkout `Map` of models in memory. Its two public non-constructor methods are:
    - `get` (lines 20–22) returns a `structuredClone` of the stored model, or an empty one.
    - `merge` (lines 25–40) merges entities and relations by `id`. If the result exceeds the entity, relation or byte limits, it rejects the whole emission. Otherwise it replaces the model in one step. When there are too many repositories, it evicts the oldest one.

The only direct call between included declarations is `parseAssistantResponse` → `scanFences`. The two methods don't call each other. I left out the constructor, the private fields, the interfaces (`ParseOptions`, `Fence`, `ModelLimits`) and the constants (`scope`, `repositoryModels`), as you asked.
